title: Erdogan Declares EU 'Not a Priority,' Vows Syria Visit and Calls Iraqi Kurds 'Brothers' in Sweeping Al Jazeera Interview
subhead: In a wide-ranging interview with Al Jazeera Arabic, President Erdogan signaled a strategic pivot away from EU accession, pledged a personal visit to Damascus, and used unprecedented language toward Kurdish communities — while hinting Egypt could join the Mecca defence pact.

sections.heading: Erdogan's Strategic Repositioning: EU Out, Regional In
sections.body: President Recep Tayyip Erdogan told Al Jazeera Arabic on August 15 that joining the European Union is 'not our priority' and that 'Europe will be the loser if Turkey does not join,' according to Izvestia's translation of the interview. He added that European countries do not demonstrate readiness for Turkey's integration, concluding Europe 'probably does not want' to include the republic. The remarks follow the EU Council's July 15 document on Turkey, Cyprus and regional security, which Ankara's Foreign Ministry called biased and the Erdogan administration said showed Brussels lacked a vision for a common future.
sections.whyItMatters: Erdogan is publicly closing the door on a decades-old accession anchor, framing Turkey's future around regional blocs rather than the EU — a shift with real consequences for trade, customs union modernization and Ankara's posture toward Brussels.

sections.heading: Kurdish 'Brothers' and a Pledge to Visit Syria
sections.body: In the same interview, Erdogan delivered what Kurdistan 24 called his most significant public statement on the Kurdish question in decades, praising Iraqi Kurds as 'our brothers' and commending the Kurdistan Region for refusing to be drawn into the US-Iran war. He also announced a personal visit to Syria 'in the coming period,' pledging Ankara will do everything to support the country's stability. The remarks pair with the AKP's peace bill filed August 5, which includes an effective pardon for former PKK fighters; Erdogan said his coalition will 'walk together' with pro-Kurdish lawmakers to pass it, following Ocalan's 2025 order for the group to disband.
sections.whyItMatters: Erdogan is attempting to convert the Kurdish question from Turkey's most persistent liability into a regional asset — but the durability of the shift depends on institutional and constitutional reforms Kurdish leaders say are the minimum for a lasting settlement.

sections.heading: Imamoglu Joins New Party as Opposition Split Consolidates
sections.body: Jailed Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu said on August 13 he was joining the newly formed New (Yeni) Party, Reuters reported, after a court order removed the leadership of his former CHP. The split began when former CHP chair Ozgur Ozel declared the New Party with 90 deputies who resigned, cutting the CHP's parliamentary group to 44 seats and stripping it of main opposition status for the first time since 2002, according to Bianet. More than 230 CHP mayors, including 28 city mayors, have since joined the New Party. The rupture stems from a May court ruling that annulled the CHP's 2023 congress and reinstated Kemal Kilicdaroglu as leader.
sections.whyItMatters: The opposition's fragmentation — driven by a court-installed leadership and a jailed presidential candidate — reshapes Turkey's political map ahead of any election, even as the New Party's rapid growth gives Erdogan's AKP a new, untested challenger.

sections.heading: Mecca Pact: Egypt's Accession Looms as Next Step
sections.body: Erdogan told Al Jazeera that expanding the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement to include Egypt represents a natural next step for broader stability, News18 reported. Egyptian officials participated in months of foundational talks alongside the three signatories — Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan — prior to the summit, laying groundwork for potential accession. The pact, signed by Erdogan, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and PM Shehbaz Sharif, carries a mutual defence commitment similar to NATO's Article 5, with a permanent secretariat based in Saudi Arabia. Bringing Egypt in would add North Africa's largest standing army to the bloc.
sections.whyItMatters: Egypt's accession would dramatically increase the pact's military weight and extend its reach across the eastern Mediterranean and Red Sea — directly relevant to Ankara's regional ambitions and its rivalry with the Cyprus-Greece-Israel axis.

sections.heading: Hyundai Launches Ioniq 3 EV Production in Turkey
sections.body: On August 14, Hyundai Motor began production of its Ioniq 3 electric vehicle at its Izmit factory in Kocaeli Province, roughly 120 km east of Istanbul, with the plant targeting the European market, according to MSN. The launch positions Turkey as a manufacturing hub for Hyundai's EV exports to Europe at a time when the EU is weighing tariffs and trade terms with Ankara.
sections.whyItMatters: The investment underscores Turkey's role as a production base for European-bound manufacturing — a counterweight to the political chill in EU relations, and a reminder that economic integration with Europe continues even as political ties fray.

bottomLine: Erdogan's Al Jazeera interview was the day's defining event: a public declaration that EU accession is no longer a priority, a pledge to visit Syria, and unprecedented language toward Kurdish communities — all framed around Turkey's post-Iran-war regional role. Domestically, the opposition's split deepened as Imamoglu joined the New Party, while the Mecca pact's potential expansion to Egypt signals Ankara's bet on a Gulf-led security architecture. The through-line is a Turkey repositioning away from its traditional Western anchor and toward regional blocs, with the Kurdish peace process as the domestic foundation for that ambition.
sources: Izvestia, Kurdistan 24, Reuters, Bianet, News18, MSN, Al Jazeera Arabic
